A student places the computer on the cooling base; in order to obtain better comfort, it is slowly adjusted from the original slot 1 to slot 4 (as shown in Figure B), and the laptop computer is always in a stationary state. Then (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The resultant force of the forces exerted by the cooling base on the computer remains unchanged

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure A, a laptop cooling base is generally provided with four slots used to adjust the angle. A student places the computer on the cooling base; in order to obtain better comfort, it is slowly adjusted from the original slot 1 to slot 4 (as shown in Figure B), and the laptop computer is always in a stationary state. During this process, how does the resultant force of the forces exerted by the cooling base on the computer change?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The resultant force of the forces exerted by the cooling base on the computer remains unchanged
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Figure A in the picture is a laptop cooling base; on the base there are slots used to adjust the support position. Figure B shows a laptop computer placed on an inclined cooling base; the inclination angle of the base is changed through different slots, and the adjustment positions from slot 1 to slot 4 are marked in the figure. Reasoning: Take the laptop computer as the object of study. The problem statement says that during the process of slowly adjusting from slot 1 to slot 4, the laptop computer is always in a stationary state, so the resultant force on the computer is always zero. The computer is subjected to its own gravity mg, directed vertically downward; it is also subjected to the total force exerted by the cooling base on the computer, namely the resultant of contact forces such as the supporting force and frictional force exerted by the base on the computer. Since the computer is stationary, the resultant force of this base action must be equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to gravity, that is, its magnitude is constantly mg and its direction is vertically upward. Adjusting the slot only changes the angle of inclination and may change the magnitudes of component forces such as the supporting force and frictional force, but their resultant still needs to balance gravity. The computer’s mass and g do not change, therefore the resultant force of the forces exerted by the cooling base on the computer remains unchanged.
